4807
# Beads Workflow Context

> **Context Recovery**: Run `bd prime` after compaction, clear, or new session
> Hooks auto-call this in Claude Code when .beads/ detected

# 🚨 SESSION CLOSE PROTOCOL 🚨

**CRITICAL**: Before saying "done" or "complete", you MUST run this checklist:

```
[ ] 1. git status              (check what changed)
[ ] 2. git add <files>         (stage code changes)
[ ] 3. git commit -m "..."     (commit code)
[ ] 4. git push                (push to remote)
```

**NEVER skip this.** Work is not done until pushed.

## Core Rules
- **Default**: Use beads for ALL task tracking (`bd create`, `bd ready`, `bd close`)
- **Prohibited**: Do NOT use TodoWrite, TaskCreate, or markdown files for task tracking
- **Workflow**: Create beads issue BEFORE writing code, mark in_progress when starting
- **Memory**: Use `bd remember "insight"` for persistent knowledge across sessions. Do NOT use MEMORY.md files — they fragment across accounts. Search with `bd memories <keyword>`.
- Persistence you don't need beats lost context
- Git workflow: beads auto-commit to Dolt, run `git push` at session end
- Session management: check `bd ready` for available work

## Essential Commands

### Finding Work
- `bd ready` - Show issues ready to work (no blockers)
- `bd list --status=open` - All open issues
- `bd list --status=in_progress` - Your active work
- `bd show <id>` - Detailed issue view with dependencies

### Creating & Updating
- `bd create --title="Summary of this issue" --description="Why this issue exists and what needs to be done" --type=task|bug|feature --priority=2` - New issue
  - Priority: 0-4 or P0-P4 (0=critical, 2=medium, 4=backlog). NOT "high"/"medium"/"low"
- `bd update <id> --claim` - Claim work
- `bd update <id> --assignee=username` - Assign to someone
- `bd update <id> --title/--description/--notes/--design` - Update fields inline
- `bd close <id>` - Mark complete
- `bd close <id1> <id2> ...` - Close multiple issues at once (more efficient)
- `bd close <id> --reason="explanation"` - Close with reason
- **Tip**: When creating multiple issues/tasks/epics, use parallel subagents for efficiency
- **WARNING**: Do NOT use `bd edit` - it opens $EDITOR (vim/nano) which blocks agents

### Dependencies & Blocking
- `bd dep add <issue> <depends-on>` - Add dependency (issue depends on depends-on)
- `bd blocked` - Show all blocked issues
- `bd show <id>` - See what's blocking/blocked by this issue

### Sync & Collaboration
- `bd dolt push` - Push beads to Dolt remote
- `bd dolt pull` - Pull beads from Dolt remote
- `bd search <query>` - Search issues by keyword

### Project Health
- `bd stats` - Project statistics (open/closed/blocked counts)
- `bd doctor` - Check for issues (sync problems, missing hooks)
- `bd doctor --check=conventions` - Check for convention drift (lint, stale, orphans)

### Quality Tools
- `bd create --validate` - Check description has required sections
- `bd create --acceptance="criteria"` - Set acceptance criteria (checked by --validate)
- `bd create --design="decisions"` - Record design decisions
- `bd create --notes="context"` - Add supplementary notes
- `bd config set validation.on-create warn` - Auto-validate on every create
- `bd lint` - Check existing issues for missing sections

### Lifecycle & Hygiene
- `bd defer <id> --until="date"` - Defer work to a future date
- `bd supersede <id> --with=<new-id>` - Mark issue as superseded
- `bd close <id> --suggest-next` - Show newly unblocked issues after closing
- `bd stale` - Find issues with no recent activity
- `bd orphans` - Find issues with broken dependencies
- `bd preflight` - Pre-PR checks (lint, stale, orphans)
- `bd human <id>` - Flag for human decision (list/respond/dismiss)

### Structured Workflows
- `bd formula list` - See available workflow templates
- `bd mol pour <name>` - Start structured workflow from formula

## Common Workflows

**Starting work:**
```bash
bd ready           # Find available work
bd show <id>       # Review issue details
bd update <id> --claim  # Claim it
```

**Completing work:**
```bash
bd close <id1> <id2> ...    # Close all completed issues at once
git add . && git commit -m "..."  # Commit code changes
git push                    # Push to remote
```

**Creating dependent work:**

content.content:
## Goal

Create a Rust symbolic execution engine for angr that initializes in Python, hands off execution to Rust for state management (memory, registers, VEX interpretation, Z3 constraint solving), and only calls back to Python for unhandled external calls (SimProcedures and syscalls).

**Why:** Python's overhead in the inner loop (state forking via deep copy, interpreted VEX execution, constraint solving via ctypes) is the bottleneck. Rust provides O(1) CoW state forking (im::OrdMap), native VEX interpretation, and direct Z3 access (z3-rs 0.19).

**How to apply:**
- Users should never need to write Rust — `RustExplorationManager` is a drop-in Python API
- Rust owns the hot path (94% time in Rust VEX+Z3, 6% in Python callbacks)
- Python only for externals (SimProcedures, syscalls) and user-facing state access
- State access from Python uses `RustStateProxy` (lightweight PyO3 wrapper), NOT full SimState reconstruction
- Architecture support: see CLAUDE.md "Architecture Support Matrix" section for current Supported/Experimental/Skeleton classification per arch (live; do not snapshot in memory).

**Test suites and live counts:** see CLAUDE.md for benchmark count, test count (`grep -c 'def test_' tests/engines/test_rust_exploration.py`), and the regression/single/full bench runners. Do not duplicate counts here — they go stale.

**Branch:** `rust-symex` (renamed/condensed from `rust-engine-v2`).

## Goal

Create a Rust symbolic execution engine for angr that initializes in Python, hands off execution to Rust for state management (memory, registers, VEX interpretation, Z3 constraint solving), and only calls back to Python for unhandled external calls (SimProcedures and syscalls).

**Why:** Python's overhead in the inner loop (state forking via deep copy, interpreted VEX execution, constraint solving via ctypes) is the bottleneck. Rust provides O(1) CoW state forking (im::OrdMap), native VEX interpretation, and direct Z3 access (z3-rs 0.19).

**How to apply:**
- Users should never need to write Rust — `RustExplorationManager` is a drop-in Python API
- Rust owns the hot path (94% time in Rust VEX+Z3, 6% in Python callbacks)
- Python only for externals (SimProcedures, syscalls) and user-facing state access
- State access from Python uses `RustStateProxy` (lightweight PyO3 wrapper), NOT full SimState reconstruction
- Architecture support: see CLAUDE.md "Architecture Support Matrix" section for current Supported/Experimental/Skeleton classification per arch (live; do not snapshot in memory).

**Test suites and live counts:** see CLAUDE.md for benchmark count, test count (`grep -c 'def test_' tests/engines/test_rust_exploration.py`), and the regression/single/full bench runners. Do not duplicate counts here — they go stale.

**Branch:** `rust-symex` (renamed/condensed from `rust-engine-v2`).

content.content:
## Rule

When the Rust engine exports a state back to a Python `SimState`, do NOT "pre-pin" tracked symbols by adding `ast == BVV(concrete)` constraints in `_sync_exported_constraints` (or anywhere else on the export path). For UNSAT-identity cases where the Python solver can't recover a symbol's value, fall back to the Rust solver via `fork_state_solver(state_id)` — that is the clean route.

## Why

History (all fixed; commits below for the archeology trail):

- `2f0e8164f` ("Remove pre-pinning constraints..."): an earlier attempt to pre-pin every tracked symbol broke `fauxware` and `flareon2015_5`. Reason: the concrete values came from `get_state_memory()` which can return *a* model rather than *the* model the rest of the solver expects. Pre-pinning then overconstrained the state with wrong values and made downstream solves UNSAT.
- `1f823ba68` ("Add Rust solver eval fallback..."): the right fix. `_attach_rust_solver_fallback` monkey-patches `state.solver.eval` to delegate to the Rust solver when Python sync would otherwise fail. This avoids touching the constraint set at all.
- `bb1a908dc` ("Fix wide symbolic import endianness..."): wide symbolic loads must use `Iend_BE` + `claripy.Reverse()` to preserve BVS identity. Loading with `Iend_LE` makes angr substitute `Reverse(original)` and silently breaks the round-trip.

## How to apply

If you find yourself adding constraints during state export to "help the Python solver", stop. That class of fix has been tried and rolled back. Instead:

1. Check that `_attach_rust_solver_fallback` is wired up on the export path you are touching. It must be attached in ALL state export paths — cached, root-copy, stepping, AND snapshot. The snapshot path was originally missed; verify no new export path repeats the bug.
2. Rust `eval` returns LE bytes — reverse with `raw[::-1]` when `cast_to=bytes`.
3. For wide symbolic imports, use `Iend_BE` + `Reverse()`; never `Iend_LE` if the original BVS identity matters.

## Pointer

For live code: `_attach_rust_solver_fallback` and `fork_state_solver` live under `angr/exploration/` (see `rust_state_export.py`, `rust_state_proxy.py`, `rust_state_cache.py`). Grep there before adding any new export path.
---
When a P3 characterization task ("investigate hackcon2016 0.9x speedup") turns up an unexpected regression (e.g., the bench actually runs 2.6x slower than the stated baseline), do BOTH:

1. Close the characterization task with docs/baseline updates per its "OR root cause documented" acceptance clause.
2. File a SEPARATE bead for the regression bisect itself, with the profile evidence and the commit-range to search.

**Why:** Characterization tasks are P3 and short — they should remain that way. Regressions are different work (bisect + revert/refactor) and may be higher priority. Conflating the two:

- Hides a real regression inside a checkbox close
- Makes the original task balloon past its time-boxing
- Loses the regression context (profile data, commit range) under the characterization's title

**How to apply:** Any time a sub-1.0x bench task surfaces that the gap is wider than expected vs the previous baseline, run `tests/benchmarks/bimodal_variance.py --benchmarks <name> --runs 10` to confirm it is unimodal (real regression) rather than bimodal (distribution variance). If unimodal: close char, file regression bead. If bimodal: close char with raised baseline + variance doc (no separate bead needed).

Pattern used 2026-05-17 on angr-hyiz.1 → angr-8t45 split.

input.content:
# Plan: Exhaustive `bd memories` Review & Prune

## Context

`bd prime` is auto-injected at the top of every Claude Code session
(`bd hooks install` configures this). It currently emits **4,807 lines /
~150 KB** — and `bd memories` has grown to **1,296 entries / ~948 KB**.
CLAUDE.md still cites the count as "987 as of 2026-05-31", so we've added
~300 memories in the last ~3 days of ralph loop activity alone.

Most of that growth is **per-iteration loop scratch** (status snapshots, "X
landed in commit Y" notes, bead-closure receipts) rather than durable
knowledge. Concretely, of 1,296 memories:

- **649** reference *only* closed beads — strong auto-forget signal once
  the body is verified to be a status note rather than a durable invariant.
- **585** reference no bead — mostly `invariant-*` (352) and `avoid-*` (116)
  durable rules; these are the highest-value entries to *retain*.
- **62** reference at least one currently-open bead — definitely keep.
- **47** are >1.5 KB; the largest is 2,962 chars — these are docs-shaped, not
  memories.
- **One cluster** (`v5a5-*`) has **46 memories** for a single bead lineage:
  iteration-by-iteration replay of a long-running ralph loop. Heavy
  duplication candidate. Similar but smaller clusters: `rust-*` (33),
  `angr-*` (19), `arch-/dead-/lazy-/disk-/gate-/neon-/pyo3-/test-*` (3-5
  each).
- **6** mention future-dated `2026-08-*` (likely typos / hallucinated dates).

Goal: prune aggressively to a leaner set (~300-500), promote the
docs-shaped memories into `docs/advanced-topics/*.rst`, and keep a
recoverable audit trail.

User-confirmed parameters (Q&A above):

1. **Bias:** aggressive — default to forget unless durable.
2. **Docs target:** append to existing `docs/advanced-topics/*.rst`; new
   stand-alone .rst only when no good home exists.
3. **Cadence:** batched with checkpoints; surface action manifest per
   batch for spot-check before applying.
4. **Audit:** archive `bd memories --json` snapshot + `.bd-prune/
   decisions.jsonl` (key + verdict + reason) for every action.

## Approach

### Phase 0 — Snapshot & scaffolding (one-time, ~5 min)

1. Snapshot: `bd memories --json > .bd-prune/snapshot-pre-prune.json`
   (gitignored — under 1 MB, recoverable).
2. Create `.bd-prune/decisions.jsonl` (append-only audit log; one JSON line
   per memory:
   `{"key":"...", "verdict":"forget|keep|promote|merge", "reason":"...",
   "promoted_to":"docs/...", "merged_into":"key", "batch":"<batch-name>"}`).
3. Create `.bd-prune/manifest-<batch>.jsonl` per batch for pre-apply review.
4. Add `.bd-prune/` to `.gitignore`.
5. Add a tiny helper script `tools/bd_prune.py` that reads the manifest and
   applies actions (`bd forget` + docs append + decisions log). Idempotent,
   resumable, dry-run by default.

### Phase 1 — Programmatic triage (heuristic bucketing, ~10 min)

For every memory, compute and tag (this is heuristic only — Phase 2 does
the actual review):

- `closed-only`: all `angr-<id>` references in body resolve to closed
  beads.
- `open-ref`: at least one bead ref is open or in_progress.
- `no-bead`: no `angr-<id>` reference (mostly invariant/avoid).
- `status-shape`: body matches `r'\b(landed|closed|merged|reverted|
  superseded|fixed in commit|completed|resolved)\b'` or starts with
  "Iter <n>" / "<date> ...".
- `docs-shape`: ≥800 chars AND contains architecture/design language
  ("architecture", "design", "how to apply", section headers, code blocks).
- `cluster-size N`: how many sibling keys share the same bead-id prefix.

# Plan: Exhaustive `bd memories` Review & Prune

## Context

`bd prime` is auto-injected at the top of every Claude Code session
(`bd hooks install` configures this). It currently emits **4,807 lines /
~150 KB** — and `bd memories` has grown to **1,296 entries / ~948 KB**.
CLAUDE.md still cites the count as "987 as of 2026-05-31", so we've added
~300 memories in the last ~3 days of ralph loop activity alone.

Most of that growth is **per-iteration loop scratch** (status snapshots, "X
landed in commit Y" notes, bead-closure receipts) rather than durable
knowledge. Concretely, of 1,296 memories:

- **649** reference *only* closed beads — strong auto-forget signal once
  the body is verified to be a status note rather than a durable invariant.
- **585** reference no bead — mostly `invariant-*` (352) and `avoid-*` (116)
  durable rules; highest-value entries to *retain*.
- **62** reference at least one currently-open bead — definitely keep.
- **47** are >1.5 KB; largest is 2,962 chars — these are docs-shaped, not
  memories.
- **One cluster** (`v5a5-*`) has **46 memories** for a single bead lineage:
  iteration-by-iteration replay of a long-running ralph loop. Heavy
  duplication candidate. Other clusters: `rust-*` (33), `angr-*` (19),
  `arch-/dead-/lazy-/disk-/gate-/neon-/pyo3-/test-*` (3-5 each).
- **6** mention future-dated `2026-08-*` (likely typos / hallucinated dates).

Goal: prune aggressively to ~300-500 memories, **promote docs-shaped
memories into `docs/advanced-topics/*.rst`**, make **CLAUDE.md the
navigational hub** (topic → docs file → bd key), and keep a recoverable
audit trail.

User-confirmed parameters:

1. **Bias:** aggressive — default to forget unless durable.
2. **Docs target:** append to existing `docs/advanced-topics/*.rst`; new
   stand-alone .rst only when no good home or target is already bloated.
3. **Cadence:** batched with checkpoints; surface action manifest per
   batch for spot-check before applying.
4. **Audit:** archive `bd memories --json` snapshot + `.bd-prune/
   decisions.jsonl` (key + verdict + reason) for every action.
5. **Navigation:** CLAUDE.md gets a new "Where context lives" subsection
   pointing readers from topic → docs file → bd memory key, so promoted
   content stays discoverable.

## Approach

### Phase 0 — Snapshot & scaffolding (one-time, ~5 min)

1. Snapshot: `bd memories --json > .bd-prune/snapshot-pre-prune.json`.
2. Create `.bd-prune/decisions.jsonl` (append-only audit log; one JSON line
   per action:
   `{"key":"...", "verdict":"forget|keep|promote|merge", "reason":"...",
   "promoted_to":"docs/...", "merged_into":"key", "batch":"<batch>"}`).
3. Create `.bd-prune/manifest-<batch>.jsonl` per batch for pre-apply review.
4. Add `.bd-prune/` to `.gitignore`.
5. Add `tools/bd_prune.py` — reads a manifest and applies actions
   (`bd forget` + docs append + decisions log). **Contract:**
   - Idempotent (re-run skips already-applied rows).
   - Resumable (state lives in `decisions.jsonl`, not in-memory).
   - Dry-run by default; `--apply` is explicit.
   - **Pre-apply validation:** refuses to run if any `--key` written by a
     `merge` row collides with a `forget` row in the same manifest, or if
     any `forget` key appears in the kept-set's `cites-graph.json`.

### Phase 1 — Programmatic triage (heuristic bucketing, ~10 min)

For every memory, compute and tag (heuristic only — Phase 2 does the actual
review):

- `closed-only`: all `angr-<id>` references in body resolve to closed
  beads.
- `open-ref`: at least one bead ref is open or in_progress.
- `no-bead`: no `angr-<id>` reference.
- `status-shape`: body matches `r'\b(landed|closed|merged|reverted|
  superseded|fixed in commit|completed|resolved)\b'` or starts with
  "Iter <n>" / "<date> ...".
- `docs-shape`: ≥800 chars AND contains architecture/design language
  ("architecture", "design", "how to apply", section headers, code blocks).
- `cluster-size N`: how many sibling keys share the same bead-id prefix.
- `stale-date`: dated body older than 2026-05-01 AND status-shape.
- `future-date`: contains a 2026-08-* date (likely typo).
- **`cites-other-memory`**: body contains backtick-quoted strings matching
  another existing memory key (`grep -F` against the key list).
- **`dup-of-claude-md`**: body fragment (≥40 char) overlaps with CLAUDE.md
  contents (e.g., venv recovery, 9.2.209 pin, build commands).
- **`dup-of-docs`**: ≥40 char fragment overlaps with any
  `docs/**/*.rst`.
- **`reference-type`**: key matches `^(bd|ralph|dolt|claude-code|git|gh|
  ci|github)-` — external-system pointers, not bead-tied.
- **`user-preference`**: body contains "user prefers" / "do not" / "always"
  with no commit reference — feedback rules.
- **`stale-file-ref`**: cites a file path that `git ls-files` cannot find.

Outputs:

- `.bd-prune/triage.csv` — key, length, tags...
- **`.bd-prune/cites-graph.json`** — `{key: [referenced_keys]}` for the
  cited-by guard in Phase 2/3.

### Phase 2 — Batched review (the big lift, ~6-10 sessions)

**Precedence:** cluster-collapse (B2) runs *first* and removes its members
from the pool before status-shape sweeps (B1*). Otherwise items in
multiple buckets get reviewed twice.

| Batch | Filter | Approx count | Heuristic verdict |
|-------|--------|--------------|-------------------|
| B2 | `cluster-size>=10` (v5a5, rust, angr) | ~100 | merge / forget (runs first) |
| B0 | `dup-of-claude-md OR dup-of-docs` | ~80 (estimate) | forget — redundant with canonical source |
| B1a | `closed-only AND status-shape` AND prefix=`v5a5` | ~40 | forget (verify each) |
| B1b | `closed-only AND status-shape` AND prefix in {rust,angr} | ~50 | forget (verify each) |
| B1c | `closed-only AND status-shape` AND `cluster-size>=3` (other) | ~150 | forget |
| B1d | `closed-only AND status-shape` (singletons) | ~150 | forget |
| B3 | `future-date` (2026-08-*) | ~6 | forget (typos) |
| B4 | `closed-only AND NOT status-shape` | ~150 | review — may contain durable rules misfiled under bead-id |
| B5 | `no-bead AND docs-shape` (size >800) | ~80 | **promote** to docs/ |
| B6 | `no-bead AND invariant-*` | ~280 | mostly keep — spot-check stale file refs |
| B7 | `no-bead AND avoid-*` | ~70 | mostly keep |
| B8 | `reference-type` + `user-preference` | ~30 | keep (verify external system still in use) |
| B9 | everything else (`open-ref`, leftover) | ~110 | review individually |

For each batch the worker (Explore agent or main agent):

1. Pulls `bd recall <key>` for each candidate.
2. Applies the rubric below (verdict + one-sentence reason).
3. Writes `.bd-prune/manifest-<batch>.jsonl`.
4. **Stops for user spot-check** before applying.
5. Once approved, runs `tools/bd_prune.py --apply manifest-<batch>.jsonl`.

#### Verdict rubric (per memory)

- **forget** when: body is a status update tied to closed work AND the
  durable lesson (if any) is captured elsewhere (CLAUDE.md, docs, another
  invariant memory); future-dated; refers to file paths that no longer
  exist; or `dup-of-claude-md` / `dup-of-docs` (canonical source wins).
- **promote** when: body is ≥500 chars of architecture/design content a
  reader without bd context would benefit from. Target file picked from
  this map:
  - Z3, solver, bv ops, AST → `docs/advanced-topics/rust_z3_sharing.rst`
  - Lazy memory, paging, CoW → `docs/advanced-topics/rust_lazy_memory_design.rst`
  - State proxy, exports, callbacks → `docs/advanced-topics/rust_proxy_writes_design.rst`
  - Bimodal benches, variance → `docs/advanced-topics/rust_bimodal_variance.rst`
  - VEX ops, interpreter, ccall → `docs/extending-angr/rust_vex_ops.rst`
  - SimProcedures → `docs/extending-angr/simprocedures.rst`
  - General engine usage, arch matrix, counters → `docs/advanced-topics/rust_engine.rst`
  - **Bloat guard:** if target file `wc -l` > **2000**, route to a sibling
    file or create `docs/internals/<topic>.rst`. `rust_engine.rst` is
    already 4252 lines — do NOT append to it without a sub-section
    justification and human review.
  - **Dup-check:** before append, `grep -F` a distinctive 40-char phrase
    from the memory body against the target file; if it hits, switch
    verdict to `forget`.
  - Include a footnote: "Originally captured 2026-XX-XX as bd memory
    `<key>`" and then `bd forget <key>`.
  - **Conversion is heuristic:** the manifest stages the RST text but the
    docs commit needs human review of headings/code-fences before merge.
- **merge** when: ≥3 sibling memories under same bead-id-prefix overlap.
  Pick the most comprehensive as canonical, append unique facts from the
  others, forget the rest. Canonical key MUST NOT appear in any forget row
  of the same manifest (bd_prune.py enforces).
- **keep** when: durable invariant; user-feedback rule; project-state
  pointer; auto-keep target of the cited-by guard (see below); or member
  of mandatory keep-list.

#### Mandatory keep-list (do not touch in any batch)

Seeded from MEMORY.md quick-keys (re-verify they still resolve at Phase 0):

- `core-goal-design-philosophy`
- `rust-proxy-architecture-decision`
- `rust-engine-claude-md-pointer`
- `rust-python-boundary-audit`
- `constraint-export-no-pre-pin`
- `characterization-vs-fix-pattern`
- `benchmark-bimodal-variance-rules`

Plus **automated additions**: any key listed in `cites-graph.json` as a
*target* of any memory that the rubric verdicts as `keep` or `promote`
gets auto-added to the keep-list. If we want to drop such a cited memory,
the rubric must also drop the citer (or rewrite it to remove the
reference). `bd_prune.py` blocks any forget that would orphan a citation.

### Phase 3 — Apply & verify (per batch, ~5 min each)

After each batch manifest is approved:

1. `python3 tools/bd_prune.py --apply .bd-prune/manifest-<batch>.jsonl`:
   - **Pre-apply validation:** reject if any `merge` canonical key
     collides with a `forget` key in this manifest; reject if any `forget`
     key is in the cited-by guard set.
   - For each `forget` row: `bd forget <key>` (skips if already removed).
   - For each `promote` row: append body (Markdown→RST conversion for
     code blocks + headings) to target .rst with footnote, then `bd forget`.
   - For each `merge` row: `bd remember --key <canonical>` with merged
     body, then `bd forget` subordinates.
   - Append each action to `.bd-prune/decisions.jsonl`.
2. Sanity-check counts: `bd memories | head -1`.
3. `bd prime > /dev/null && echo ok` to confirm no crashes.
4. `git diff docs/ --stat` — flag any single file growing >500 lines.
5. Manual review of promoted RST chunks; fix heading/code-fence drift.
6. Commit docs/ additions: one commit per batch with summary
   "prune: B<n> — promoted N memories, forgot M". Memory removal is
   recorded in Dolt automatically.

### Phase 4 — Final cleanup & navigation hub (~15 min)

This phase reshapes CLAUDE.md so it remains the entry point for context
that used to live in bd memories.

1. **CLAUDE.md "Memory system" section:**
   - Refresh count line → live count.
   - Expand quick-keys list to also include keys already cited inline
     elsewhere in CLAUDE.md: `env-venv-corruption`,
     `bd-update-notes-overwrites`, `9maq-bisect-method`,
     `venv-rebuild-cargo-direct-copy`, `avoid-pip-install-deps`. Verify
     each still resolves after Phase 3.
2. **CLAUDE.md new subsection "Where context lives"** — a short table
   readers (and future agents) scan first when they need background:

   ```
   | Topic                          | Docs                                                      | bd memory key (entry point)         |
   |--------------------------------|-----------------------------------------------------------|-------------------------------------|
   | Engine architecture & usage    | docs/advanced-topics/rust_engine.rst                      | core-goal-design-philosophy         |
   | Z3 sharing & solver counters   | docs/advanced-topics/rust_z3_sharing.rst                  | constraint-export-no-pre-pin        |
   | Lazy memory design             | docs/advanced-topics/rust_lazy_memory_design.rst          | (per docs)                          |
   | State proxy & exports          | docs/advanced-topics/rust_proxy_writes_design.rst         | rust-proxy-architecture-decision    |
   | Bimodal benchmark variance     | docs/advanced-topics/rust_bimodal_variance.rst            | benchmark-bimodal-variance-rules    |
   | VEX op contribution            | docs/extending-angr/rust_vex_ops.rst                      | (per docs)                          |
   | Native SimProcedures           | docs/extending-angr/simprocedures.rst                     | (per docs)                          |
   ```

   The table is one short paragraph in CLAUDE.md; full details live in the
   linked docs. Add a one-liner above the table: "When you need context
   that isn't in CLAUDE.md, look here first, then `bd recall`."

3. **MEMORY.md reconciliation:**
   - MEMORY.md currently says "977 memories" — drift. Either: (a) refresh
     it to match the new count, or (b) replace its body with a stub
     pointing at CLAUDE.md's new "Where context lives" subsection.
   - Recommendation: (b). MEMORY.md exists only because the auto-memory
     prompt expects it; per CLAUDE.md, bd is canonical. The stub keeps
     the auto-memory machinery happy without inviting drift.

4. `bd prime | wc -l && bd prime | wc -c` — confirm reductions.
5. Final snapshot: `bd memories --json > .bd-prune/snapshot-post-prune.json`.
6. Write `.bd-prune/README.md` explaining recovery: how to mine
   `snapshot-pre-prune.json` if a forgotten memory turns out to have been
   load-bearing.

# Plan: Exhaustive `bd memories` Review & Prune

## Context

`bd prime` is auto-injected at the top of every Claude Code session
(`bd hooks install` configures this). It currently emits **4,807 lines /
~150 KB** — and `bd memories` has grown to **1,296 entries / ~948 KB**.
CLAUDE.md still cites the count as "987 as of 2026-05-31", so we've added
~300 memories in the last ~3 days of ralph loop activity alone.

Most of that growth is **per-iteration loop scratch** (status snapshots, "X
landed in commit Y" notes, bead-closure receipts) rather than durable
knowledge. Concretely, of 1,296 memories:

- **649** reference *only* closed beads — strong auto-forget signal once
  the body is verified to be a status note rather than a durable invariant.
- **585** reference no bead — mostly `invariant-*` (352) and `avoid-*` (116)
  durable rules; highest-value entries to *retain*.
- **62** reference at least one currently-open bead — definitely keep.
- **47** are >1.5 KB; largest is 2,962 chars — these are docs-shaped, not
  memories.
- **One cluster** (`v5a5-*`) has **46 memories** for a single bead lineage:
  iteration-by-iteration replay of a long-running ralph loop. Heavy
  duplication candidate. Other clusters: `rust-*` (33), `angr-*` (19),
  `arch-/dead-/lazy-/disk-/gate-/neon-/pyo3-/test-*` (3-5 each).
- **6** mention future-dated `2026-08-*` (likely typos / hallucinated dates).

Goal: prune aggressively to ~300-500 memories, **promote docs-shaped
memories into `docs/advanced-topics/*.rst`**, make **CLAUDE.md the
navigational hub** (topic → docs file → bd key), and keep a recoverable
audit trail.

User-confirmed parameters:

1. **Bias:** aggressive — default to forget unless durable.
2. **Docs target:** append to existing `docs/advanced-topics/*.rst`; new
   stand-alone .rst only when no good home or target is already bloated.
3. **Cadence:** batched with checkpoints; surface action manifest per
   batch for spot-check before applying.
4. **Audit:** archive `bd memories --json` snapshot + `.bd-prune/
   decisions.jsonl` (key + verdict + reason) for every action.
5. **Navigation:** CLAUDE.md gets a new "Where context lives" subsection
   pointing readers from topic → docs file → bd memory key, so promoted
   content stays discoverable.

## Approach

### Phase 0 — Snapshot & scaffolding (one-time, ~5 min)

1. Snapshot: `bd memories --json > .bd-prune/snapshot-pre-prune.json`.
2. Create `.bd-prune/decisions.jsonl` (append-only audit log; one JSON line
   per action:
   `{"key":"...", "verdict":"forget|keep|promote|merge", "reason":"...",
   "promoted_to":"docs/...", "merged_into":"key", "batch":"<batch>"}`).
3. Create `.bd-prune/manifest-<batch>.jsonl` per batch for pre-apply review.
4. Add `.bd-prune/` to `.gitignore`.
5. Add `tools/bd_prune.py` — reads a manifest and applies actions
   (`bd forget` + docs append + decisions log). **Contract:**
   - Idempotent (re-run skips already-applied rows).
   - Resumable (state lives in `decisions.jsonl`, not in-memory).
   - Dry-run by default; `--apply` is explicit.
   - **Pre-apply validation:** refuses to run if any `--key` written by a
     `merge` row collides with a `forget` row in the same manifest, or if
     any `forget` key appears in the kept-set's `cites-graph.json`.

### Phase 1 — Programmatic triage (heuristic bucketing, ~10 min)

For every memory, compute and tag (heuristic only — Phase 2 does the actual
review):

- `closed-only`: all `angr-<id>` references in body resolve to closed
  beads.
- `open-ref`: at least one bead ref is open or in_progress.
- `no-bead`: no `angr-<id>` reference.
- `status-shape`: body matches `r'\b(landed|closed|merged|reverted|
  superseded|fixed in commit|completed|resolved)\b'` or starts with
  "Iter <n>" / "<date> ...".
- `docs-shape`: ≥800 chars AND contains architecture/design language
  ("architecture", "design", "how to apply", section headers, code blocks).
- `cluster-size N`: how many sibling keys share the same bead-id prefix.
- `stale-date`: dated body older than 2026-05-01 AND status-shape.
- `future-date`: contains a 2026-08-* date (likely typo).
- **`cites-other-memory`**: body contains backtick-quoted strings matching
  another existing memory key (`grep -F` against the key list).
- **`dup-of-claude-md`**: body fragment (≥40 char) overlaps with CLAUDE.md
  contents (e.g., venv recovery, 9.2.209 pin, build commands).
- **`dup-of-docs`**: ≥40 char fragment overlaps with any
  `docs/**/*.rst`.
- **`reference-type`**: key matches `^(bd|ralph|dolt|claude-code|git|gh|
  ci|github)-` — external-system pointers, not bead-tied.
- **`user-preference`**: body contains "user prefers" / "do not" / "always"
  with no commit reference — feedback rules.
- **`stale-file-ref`**: cites a file path that `git ls-files` cannot find.

Outputs:

- `.bd-prune/triage.csv` — key, length, tags...
- **`.bd-prune/cites-graph.json`** — `{key: [referenced_keys]}` for the
  cited-by guard in Phase 2/3.

### Phase 2 — Batched review (the big lift, ~6-10 sessions)

**Precedence:** cluster-collapse (B2) runs *first* and removes its members
from the pool before status-shape sweeps (B1*). Otherwise items in
multiple buckets get reviewed twice.

| Batch | Filter | Approx count | Heuristic verdict |
|-------|--------|--------------|-------------------|
| B2 | `cluster-size>=10` (v5a5, rust, angr) | ~100 | merge / forget (runs first) |
| B0 | `dup-of-claude-md OR dup-of-docs` | ~80 (estimate) | forget — redundant with canonical source |
| B1a | `closed-only AND status-shape` AND prefix=`v5a5` | ~40 | forget (verify each) |
| B1b | `closed-only AND status-shape` AND prefix in {rust,angr} | ~50 | forget (verify each) |
| B1c | `closed-only AND status-shape` AND `cluster-size>=3` (other) | ~150 | forget |
| B1d | `closed-only AND status-shape` (singletons) | ~150 | forget |
| B3 | `future-date` (2026-08-*) | ~6 | forget (typos) |
| B4 | `closed-only AND NOT status-shape` | ~150 | review — may contain durable rules misfiled under bead-id |
| B5 | `no-bead AND docs-shape` (size >800) | ~80 | **promote** to docs/ |
| B6 | `no-bead AND invariant-*` | ~280 | mostly keep — spot-check stale file refs |
| B7 | `no-bead AND avoid-*` | ~70 | mostly keep |
| B8 | `reference-type` + `user-preference` | ~30 | keep (verify external system still in use) |
| B9 | everything else (`open-ref`, leftover) | ~110 | review individually |

For each batch the worker (Explore agent or main agent):

1. Pulls `bd recall <key>` for each candidate.
2. Applies the rubric below (verdict + one-sentence reason).
3. Writes `.bd-prune/manifest-<batch>.jsonl`.
4. **Stops for user spot-check** before applying.
5. Once approved, runs `tools/bd_prune.py --apply manifest-<batch>.jsonl`.

#### Verdict rubric (per memory)

- **forget** when: body is a status update tied to closed work AND the
  durable lesson (if any) is captured elsewhere (CLAUDE.md, docs, another
  invariant memory); future-dated; refers to file paths that no longer
  exist; or `dup-of-claude-md` / `dup-of-docs` (canonical source wins).
- **promote** when: body is ≥500 chars of architecture/design content a
  reader without bd context would benefit from. Target file picked from
  this map:
  - Z3, solver, bv ops, AST → `docs/advanced-topics/rust_z3_sharing.rst`
  - Lazy memory, paging, CoW → `docs/advanced-topics/rust_lazy_memory_design.rst`
  - State proxy, exports, callbacks → `docs/advanced-topics/rust_proxy_writes_design.rst`
  - Bimodal benches, variance → `docs/advanced-topics/rust_bimodal_variance.rst`
  - VEX ops, interpreter, ccall → `docs/extending-angr/rust_vex_ops.rst`
  - SimProcedures → `docs/extending-angr/simprocedures.rst`
  - General engine usage, arch matrix, counters → `docs/advanced-topics/rust_engine.rst`
  - **Bloat guard:** if target file `wc -l` > **2000**, route to a sibling
    file or create `docs/internals/<topic>.rst`. `rust_engine.rst` is
    already 4252 lines — do NOT append to it without a sub-section
    justification and human review.
  - **Dup-check:** before append, `grep -F` a distinctive 40-char phrase
    from the memory body against the target file; if it hits, switch
    verdict to `forget`.
  - Include a footnote: "Originally captured 2026-XX-XX as bd memory
    `<key>`" and then `bd forget <key>`.
  - **Conversion is heuristic:** the manifest stages the RST text but the
    docs commit needs human review of headings/code-fences before merge.
- **merge** when: ≥3 sibling memories under same bead-id-prefix overlap.
  Pick the most comprehensive as canonical, append unique facts from the
  others, forget the rest. Canonical key MUST NOT appear in any forget row
  of the same manifest (bd_prune.py enforces).
- **keep** when: durable invariant; user-feedback rule; project-state
  pointer; auto-keep target of the cited-by guard (see below); or member
  of mandatory keep-list.

#### Mandatory keep-list (do not touch in any batch)

Seeded from MEMORY.md quick-keys (re-verify they still resolve at Phase 0):

- `core-goal-design-philosophy`
- `rust-proxy-architecture-decision`
- `rust-engine-claude-md-pointer`

- `constraint-export-no-pre-pin`

gets auto-added to the keep-list. If we want to drop such a cited memory,
the rubric must also drop the citer (or rewrite it to remove the
reference). `bd_prune.py` blocks any forget that would orphan a citation.

### Phase 3 — Apply & verify (per batch, ~5 min each)

After each batch manifest is approved:

1. `python3 tools/bd_prune.py --apply .bd-prune/manifest-<batch>.jsonl`:
   - **Pre-apply validation:** reject if any `merge` canonical key
     collides with a `forget` key in this manifest; reject if any `forget`
     key is in the cited-by guard set.

6. Commit docs/ additions: one commit per batch with summary
   "prune: B<n> — promoted N memories, forgot M". Memory removal is
   recorded in Dolt automatically.

### Phase 4 — Final cleanup & navigation hub (~15 min)

This phase reshapes CLAUDE.md so it remains the entry point for context
that used to live in bd memories.

1. **CLAUDE.md "Memory system" section:**
   - Refresh count line → live count.
   - Expand quick-keys list to also include keys already cited inline
     elsewhere in CLAUDE.md: `env-venv-corruption`,

# Plan: Exhaustive `bd memories` Review & Prune

## Context

`bd prime` is auto-injected at the top of every Claude Code session
(`bd hooks install` configures this). It currently emits **4,807 lines /
~150 KB** — and `bd memories` has grown to **1,296 entries / ~948 KB**.
CLAUDE.md still cites the count as "987 as of 2026-05-31", so we've added
~300 memories in the last ~3 days of ralph loop activity alone.

Most of that growth is **per-iteration loop scratch** (status snapshots, "X
landed in commit Y" notes, bead-closure receipts) rather than durable
knowledge. Concretely, of 1,296 memories:

- **649** reference *only* closed beads — strong auto-forget signal once
  the body is verified to be a status note rather than a durable invariant.
- **585** reference no bead — mostly `invariant-*` (352) and `avoid-*` (116)
  durable rules; highest-value entries to *retain*.
- **62** reference at least one currently-open bead — definitely keep.
- **47** are >1.5 KB; largest is 2,962 chars — these are docs-shaped, not
  memories.
- **One cluster** (`v5a5-*`) has **46 memories** for a single bead lineage:
  iteration-by-iteration replay of a long-running ralph loop. Heavy
  duplication candidate. Other clusters: `rust-*` (33), `angr-*` (19),
  `arch-/dead-/lazy-/disk-/gate-/neon-/pyo3-/test-*` (3-5 each).
- **6** mention future-dated `2026-08-*` (likely typos / hallucinated dates).

Goal: prune aggressively to ~300-500 memories, **promote docs-shaped
memories into `docs/advanced-topics/*.rst`**, make **CLAUDE.md the
navigational hub** (topic → docs file → bd key), and keep a recoverable
audit trail.

User-confirmed parameters:

1. **Bias:** aggressive — default to forget unless durable.
2. **Docs target:** append to existing `docs/advanced-topics/*.rst`; new
   stand-alone .rst only when no good home or target is already bloated.
3. **Cadence:** batched with checkpoints; surface action manifest per
   batch for spot-check before applying.
4. **Audit:** archive `bd memories --json` snapshot + `.bd-prune/
   decisions.jsonl` (key + verdict + reason) for every action.
5. **Navigation:** CLAUDE.md gets a new "Where context lives" subsection
   pointing readers from topic → docs file → bd memory key, so promoted
   content stays discoverable.

## Approach

### Phase 0 — Snapshot & scaffolding (one-time, ~5 min)

1. Snapshot: `bd memories --json > .bd-prune/snapshot-pre-prune.json`.
2. Create `.bd-prune/decisions.jsonl` (append-only audit log; one JSON line
   per action:
   `{"key":"...", "verdict":"forget|keep|promote|merge", "reason":"...",
   "promoted_to":"docs/...", "merged_into":"key", "batch":"<batch>"}`).
3. Create `.bd-prune/manifest-<batch>.jsonl` per batch for pre-apply review.
4. Add `.bd-prune/` to `.gitignore`.
5. Add `tools/bd_prune.py` — reads a manifest and applies actions
   (`bd forget` + docs append + decisions log). **Contract:**
   - Idempotent (re-run skips already-applied rows).
   - Resumable (state lives in `decisions.jsonl`, not in-memory).
   - Dry-run by default; `--apply` is explicit.
   - **Pre-apply validation:** refuses to run if any `--key` written by a
     `merge` row collides with a `forget` row in the same manifest, or if
     any `forget` key appears in the kept-set's `cites-graph.json`.

### Phase 1 — Programmatic triage (heuristic bucketing, ~10 min)

For every memory, compute and tag (heuristic only — Phase 2 does the actual
review):

- `closed-only`: all `angr-<id>` references in body resolve to closed
  beads.
- `open-ref`: at least one bead ref is open or in_progress.
- `no-bead`: no `angr-<id>` reference.
- `status-shape`: body matches `r'\b(landed|closed|merged|reverted|
  superseded|fixed in commit|completed|resolved)\b'` or starts with
  "Iter <n>" / "<date> ...".
- `docs-shape`: ≥800 chars AND contains architecture/design language
  ("architecture", "design", "how to apply", section headers, code blocks).
- `cluster-size N`: how many sibling keys share the same bead-id prefix.
- `stale-date`: dated body older than 2026-05-01 AND status-shape.
- `future-date`: contains a 2026-08-* date (likely typo).
- **`cites-other-memory`**: body contains backtick-quoted strings matching
  another existing memory key (`grep -F` against the key list).
- **`dup-of-claude-md`**: body fragment (≥40 char) overlaps with CLAUDE.md
  contents (e.g., venv recovery, 9.2.209 pin, build commands).
- **`dup-of-docs`**: ≥40 char fragment overlaps with any
  `docs/**/*.rst`.
- **`reference-type`**: key matches `^(bd|ralph|dolt|claude-code|git|gh|
  ci|github)-` — external-system pointers, not bead-tied.
- **`user-preference`**: body contains "user prefers" / "do not" / "always"
  with no commit reference — feedback rules.
- **`stale-file-ref`**: cites a file path that `git ls-files` cannot find.

Outputs:

- `.bd-prune/triage.csv` — key, length, tags...
- **`.bd-prune/cites-graph.json`** — `{key: [referenced_keys]}` for the
  cited-by guard in Phase 2/3.

### Phase 2 — Batched review (the big lift, ~6-10 sessions)

**Precedence:** cluster-collapse (B2) runs *first* and removes its members
from the pool before status-shape sweeps (B1*). Otherwise items in
multiple buckets get reviewed twice.

| Batch | Filter | Approx count | Heuristic verdict |
|-------|--------|--------------|-------------------|
| B2 | `cluster-size>=10` (v5a5, rust, angr) | ~100 | merge / forget (runs first) |
| B0 | `dup-of-claude-md OR dup-of-docs` | ~80 (estimate) | forget — redundant with canonical source |
| B1a | `closed-only AND status-shape` AND prefix=`v5a5` | ~40 | forget (verify each) |
| B1b | `closed-only AND status-shape` AND prefix in {rust,angr} | ~50 | forget (verify each) |
| B1c | `closed-only AND status-shape` AND `cluster-size>=3` (other) | ~150 | forget |
| B1d | `closed-only AND status-shape` (singletons) | ~150 | forget |
| B3 | `future-date` (2026-08-*) | ~6 | forget (typos) |
| B4 | `closed-only AND NOT status-shape` | ~150 | review — may contain durable rules misfiled under bead-id |
| B5 | `no-bead AND docs-shape` (size >800) | ~80 | **promote** to docs/ |
| B6 | `no-bead AND invariant-*` | ~280 | mostly keep — spot-check stale file refs |
| B7 | `no-bead AND avoid-*` | ~70 | mostly keep |
| B8 | `reference-type` + `user-preference` | ~30 | keep (verify external system still in use) |

1. Pulls `bd recall <key>` for each candidate.
2. Applies the rubric below (verdict + one-sentence reason).
3. Writes `.bd-prune/manifest-<batch>.jsonl`.

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""Apply a bd-memories prune manifest.

Reads a manifest JSONL (one decision per line) and executes the actions:

  - "forget"   -> bd forget <key>
  - "promote"  -> append body (best-effort RST conversion) to a docs file,
                  then bd forget <key>
  - "merge"    -> bd remember --key <canonical> <merged-body>, then
                  bd forget on each subordinate key
  - "keep"     -> no-op (logged for completeness)

Safety contract:

  * Dry-run by default. Use `--apply` to actually mutate bd.
  * Idempotent: an action whose `key` already appears in
    `.bd-prune/decisions.jsonl` with the same verdict is skipped on rerun.
  * Pre-apply validation:
      - reject if any merge `canonical` collides with a forget `key` in the
        manifest
      - reject if any forget `key` is listed as a target in
        `.bd-prune/cites-graph.json` for a memory we intend to keep/promote
  * Every applied action is appended to `.bd-prune/decisions.jsonl`.

Manifest row schema (JSON object per line):

  {
    "key":           "<memory key>",
    "verdict":       "forget" | "keep" | "promote" | "merge",
    "reason":        "<short reason>",
    "batch":         "B0|B1a|...",

    # promote-only:
    "promoted_to":   "docs/advanced-topics/<file>.rst",
    "body":          "<RST-converted body to append>",

    # merge-only:
    "merged_into":   "<canonical key>",       # on subordinates
    "canonical":     true,                     # on the canonical row
    "merged_body":   "<full merged body>",     # on canonical row
  }
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import argparse
import datetime as dt
import json
import re
import subprocess
import sys
from pathlib import Path
from typing import Any

PRUNE_DIR = Path(".bd-prune")
DECISIONS = PRUNE_DIR / "decisions.jsonl"
CITES_GRAPH = PRUNE_DIR / "cites-graph.json"


def _run(cmd: list[str], *, check: bool = True) -> subprocess.CompletedProcess:
    return subprocess.run(cmd, check=check, capture_output=True, text=True)


def _load_decisions() -> set[tuple[str, str]]:
    if not DECISIONS.exists():
        return set()
    seen: set[tuple[str, str]] = set()
    for line in DECISIONS.read_text().splitlines():
        line = line.strip()
        if not line:
            continue
        rec = json.loads(line)
        seen.add((rec["key"], rec["verdict"]))
    return seen


def _append_decision(rec: dict[str, Any]) -> None:
    rec = {**rec, "applied_at": dt.datetime.utcnow().isoformat() + "Z"}
    with DECISIONS.open("a") as f:
        f.write(json.dumps(rec, ensure_ascii=False) + "\n")


def _load_manifest(path: Path) -> list[dict[str, Any]]:
    rows: list[dict[str, Any]] = []
    for ln in path.read_text().splitlines():
        ln = ln.strip()
        if not ln or ln.startswith("#"):
            continue
        rows.append(json.loads(ln))
    return rows


def _load_cites_guard() -> set[str]:
    if not CITES_GRAPH.exists():
        return set()
    # cites-graph.json: {citer_key: [cited_keys, ...]}
    graph = json.loads(CITES_GRAPH.read_text())
    guard: set[str] = set()
    for cited in graph.values():
        guard.update(cited)
    return guard


def validate(manifest: list[dict[str, Any]], cites_guard: set[str]) -> list[str]:
    """Return a list of validation errors (empty = ok)."""
    errors: list[str] = []
    forget_keys = {r["key"] for r in manifest if r["verdict"] == "forget"}
    merge_canonical = {
        r.get("merged_into") for r in manifest
        if r["verdict"] == "merge" and not r.get("canonical")
    }
    merge_canonical |= {r["key"] for r in manifest if r["verdict"] == "merge" and r.get("canonical")}

    # collision: a canonical we are writing should not also be forgotten
    collisions = forget_keys & merge_canonical
    if collisions:
        errors.append(
            f"merge canonical collides with forget rows: {sorted(collisions)}"
        )

    # cited-by guard: any forget key cited by a kept memory is a problem
    if cites_guard:
        orphans = forget_keys & cites_guard
        if orphans:
            errors.append(
                f"forget would orphan cited keys: {sorted(orphans)} "
                f"(see {CITES_GRAPH})"
            )
    return errors


_HEADING_RE = re.compile(r"^(#{1,4})\s+(.+?)\s*$")
_FENCE_RE = re.compile(r"^```([a-zA-Z0-9_+-]*)$")


def md_to_rst(body: str) -> str:
    """Crude Markdown -> RST conversion for memory bodies.

    Memory bodies are usually informal prose with the occasional `code`
    span or fenced block. This handles:
      - ATX headings (#, ##, ###) -> RST underlines
      - Fenced code blocks ``` -> RST literal block (.. code-block::)
      - Bullet lists pass through unchanged
      - Backtick spans stay as-is (RST accepts them)
    Human review in the docs commit is required for anything fancier.
    """
    out_lines: list[str] = []
    in_fence = False
    fence_lang = ""
    for raw in body.splitlines():
        if (m := _FENCE_RE.match(raw)):
            if not in_fence:
                fence_lang = m.group(1) or "text"
                out_lines.append("")
                out_lines.append(f".. code-block:: {fence_lang}")
                out_lines.append("")
                in_fence = True
            else:
                out_lines.append("")
                in_fence = False
            continue
        if in_fence:
            out_lines.append(f"    {raw}")
            continue
        if (m := _HEADING_RE.match(raw)):
            level = len(m.group(1))
            title = m.group(2)
            char = {1: "=", 2: "-", 3: "~", 4: "."}.get(level, "-")
            out_lines.append("")
            out_lines.append(title)
            out_lines.append(char * max(len(title), 3))
            out_lines.append("")
            continue
        out_lines.append(raw)
    return "\n".join(out_lines).rstrip() + "\n"


def do_forget(row: dict[str, Any], apply: bool) -> None:
    key = row["key"]
    if apply:
        cp = _run(["bd", "forget", key], check=False)
        if cp.returncode != 0:
            print(f"  WARN: bd forget {key} exit={cp.returncode}: "
                  f"{cp.stderr.strip()}", file=sys.stderr)
        _append_decision(row)
    else:
        print(f"  [dry] bd forget {key}")


def do_promote(row: dict[str, Any], apply: bool) -> None:
    key = row["key"]
    target = Path(row["promoted_to"])
    body = row.get("body") or ""
    rst = md_to_rst(body)
    today = dt.date.today().isoformat()
    footer = (
        f"\n.. note::\n\n   Originally captured {today} as bd memory ``{key}``.\n"
    )
    chunk = "\n" + rst + footer

    # bloat guard
    if target.exists():
        line_count = sum(1 for _ in target.open())
        if line_count > 2000 and not row.get("override_bloat_guard"):
            print(f"  SKIP promote -> {target}: file has {line_count} lines "
                  f"(>2000 bloat guard). Set override_bloat_guard=true to force.",
                  file=sys.stderr)
            return

    # dup-check: distinctive phrase
    if target.exists() and body.strip():
        phrase = body.strip().split("\n")[0][:60]
        if phrase and phrase in target.read_text():
            print(f"  SKIP promote -> {target}: target already contains "
                  f"distinctive phrase {phrase!r}; verdict downgraded to forget.",
                  file=sys.stderr)
            if apply:
                do_forget({**row, "verdict": "forget",
                           "reason": "dup-of-docs (auto-detected during apply)"},
                          apply=apply)
            return

    if apply:
        with target.open("a") as f:
            f.write(chunk)
        cp = _run(["bd", "forget", key], check=False)
        if cp.returncode != 0:
            print(f"  WARN: bd forget {key} exit={cp.returncode}: "
                  f"{cp.stderr.strip()}", file=sys.stderr)
        _append_decision(row)
    else:
        print(f"  [dry] append {len(chunk)} chars to {target}, then bd forget {key}")


def do_merge_canonical(row: dict[str, Any], apply: bool) -> None:
    key = row["key"]
    body = row["merged_body"]
    if apply:
        cp = _run(["bd", "remember", body, "--key", key], check=False)
        if cp.returncode != 0:
            print(f"  ERROR: bd remember --key {key} exit={cp.returncode}: "
                  f"{cp.stderr.strip()}", file=sys.stderr)
            return
        _append_decision(row)
    else:
        print(f"  [dry] bd remember --key {key} <{len(body)}-char body>")


def do_merge_subordinate(row: dict[str, Any], apply: bool) -> None:
    # subordinates of a merge are forgotten — same semantics as forget
    do_forget({**row, "verdict": "merge"}, apply=apply)


def do_keep(row: dict[str, Any], apply: bool) -> None:
    if apply:
        _append_decision(row)
    else:
        print(f"  [dry] keep {row['key']} ({row.get('reason', '')})")


def apply_manifest(path: Path, apply: bool) -> int:
    manifest = _load_manifest(path)
    print(f"Manifest: {path} ({len(manifest)} rows)")

    cites_guard = _load_cites_guard()
    errors = validate(manifest, cites_guard)
    if errors:
        print("VALIDATION ERRORS:", file=sys.stderr)
        for e in errors:
            print(f"  - {e}", file=sys.stderr)
        return 2

    seen = _load_decisions()
    counts = {"forget": 0, "promote": 0, "merge": 0, "keep": 0, "skip": 0}

    for row in manifest:
        key = row["key"]
        verdict = row["verdict"]
        if (key, verdict) in seen:
            counts["skip"] += 1
            continue
        if verdict == "forget":
            do_forget(row, apply)
            counts["forget"] += 1
        elif verdict == "promote":
            do_promote(row, apply)
            counts["promote"] += 1
        elif verdict == "merge":
            if row.get("canonical"):
                do_merge_canonical(row, apply)
            else:
                do_merge_subordinate(row, apply)
            counts["merge"] += 1
        elif verdict == "keep":
            do_keep(row, apply)
            counts["keep"] += 1
        else:
            print(f"  WARN: unknown verdict {verdict!r} for {key}",
                  file=sys.stderr)

    mode = "applied" if apply else "dry-run"
    print(f"\n{mode}: forget={counts['forget']} promote={counts['promote']} "
          f"merge={counts['merge']} keep={counts['keep']} "
          f"skipped(already-applied)={counts['skip']}")
    return 0


def main() -> int:
    ap = argparse.ArgumentParser(description=__doc__.splitlines()[0])
    ap.add_argument("manifest", type=Path, help="path to manifest JSONL")
    ap.add_argument("--apply", action="store_true",
                    help="actually mutate bd (default: dry-run)")
    args = ap.parse_args()
    if not args.manifest.exists():
        print(f"manifest not found: {args.manifest}", file=sys.stderr)
        return 1
    if not PRUNE_DIR.exists():
        PRUNE_DIR.mkdir(parents=True)
    return apply_manifest(args.manifest, args.apply)


if __name__ == "__main__":
    raise SystemExit(main())

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""Phase 1 triage: bucket every bd memory by heuristic tags.

Reads `.bd-prune/snapshot-pre-prune.json` (full memory dump) and emits:

  .bd-prune/triage.csv         — key, length, tags, prefix, cluster_size
  .bd-prune/cites-graph.json   — {citer: [cited_keys, ...]}

Tags (all boolean unless noted):

  closed-only       all `angr-<id>` refs resolve to closed beads
  open-ref          at least one bead ref is open/in_progress/blocked
  no-bead           no `angr-<id>` reference
  status-shape      body matches landed|closed|merged|reverted|... or starts
                    with "Iter <n>" / "<YYYY-MM-DD> ..."
  docs-shape        >=800 chars with arch/design language or RST/MD headings
  future-date       contains 2026-08-* or later date
  stale-date        most recent date in body < 2026-05-01 AND status-shape
  cites-other       body contains the literal key of another bd memory
  dup-of-claude-md  >=40-char fragment from body present in CLAUDE.md
  dup-of-docs       >=40-char fragment from body present in any docs/**/*.rst
  reference-type    key prefix matches bd|ralph|dolt|claude-code|git|gh|ci|github
  user-preference   body contains "user prefers" / "do not" / "always" w/o commit
  stale-file-ref    cites a path that git ls-files cannot resolve
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import csv
import json
import re
import subprocess
from pathlib import Path
from typing import Any

ROOT = Path(".")
PRUNE_DIR = ROOT / ".bd-prune"
SNAPSHOT = PRUNE_DIR / "snapshot-pre-prune.json"
TRIAGE_CSV = PRUNE_DIR / "triage.csv"
CITES_JSON = PRUNE_DIR / "cites-graph.json"

BEAD_RE = re.compile(r"\bangr-([a-z0-9]+)(?:\.\d+)?\b")
DATE_RE = re.compile(r"\b(20\d\d)-(\d\d)-(\d\d)\b")
STATUS_RE = re.compile(
    r"\b(landed|closed|merged|reverted|superseded|fixed in commit|completed|resolved)\b",
    re.I,
)
ITER_START_RE = re.compile(r"^\s*(iter\s+\d|20\d\d-\d\d-\d\d)\b", re.I)
DOCS_LANG_RE = re.compile(
    r"\b(architecture|design|how to apply|invariant|rule|why:|how:|##\s|```)",
    re.I,
)
USER_PREF_RE = re.compile(r"\b(user prefers|do not|don.t |never |always )\b", re.I)
REF_TYPE_PREFIXES = ("bd-", "ralph-", "dolt-", "claude-code-",
                     "git-", "gh-", "ci-", "github-")
FILE_PATH_RE = re.compile(
    r"(?<![\w-])(?:angr|native|tests|docs|tools)/[A-Za-z0-9_./-]+\.[A-Za-z]+",
)


def _load_bead_status() -> dict[str, str]:
    """Return {bead_id: status} for all beads."""
    out: dict[str, str] = {}
    for status in ("open", "in_progress", "blocked", "deferred", "closed"):
        try:
            cp = subprocess.run(
                ["bd", "list", f"--status={status}", "--limit=0", "--json"],
                check=True, capture_output=True, text=True,
            )
        except subprocess.CalledProcessError:
            continue
        for item in json.loads(cp.stdout or "[]"):
            out[item["id"]] = status
    return out


def _load_repo_files() -> set[str]:
    cp = subprocess.run(["git", "ls-files"], check=True,
                        capture_output=True, text=True)
    return set(cp.stdout.splitlines())


def _load_claude_md() -> str:
    return Path("CLAUDE.md").read_text()


def _load_all_docs_text() -> str:
    parts: list[str] = []
    for p in Path("docs").rglob("*.rst"):
        parts.append(p.read_text())
    return "\n".join(parts)


def _fragments(body: str, n: int = 40, max_samples: int = 12) -> list[str]:
    """Sample fragments from body for dup detection."""
    body = body.strip()
    if len(body) < n:
        return [body] if body else []
    step = max(len(body) // max_samples, n)
    frags = []
    for i in range(0, len(body) - n, step):
        frag = body[i:i + n].strip()
        if len(frag) >= n and not frag.startswith("```"):
            frags.append(frag)
        if len(frags) >= max_samples:
            break
    return frags


def main() -> int:
    if not SNAPSHOT.exists():
        raise SystemExit(f"missing {SNAPSHOT}")
    mems: dict[str, str] = json.loads(SNAPSHOT.read_text())
    bead_status = _load_bead_status()
    repo_files = _load_repo_files()
    claude_md = _load_claude_md()
    docs_text = _load_all_docs_text()

    # cluster size by bead-id prefix and free-form prefix
    prefix_counts: dict[str, int] = {}
    for k in mems:
        # extract first hyphen-separated token as the "prefix"
        pfx = k.split("-")[0]
        prefix_counts[pfx] = prefix_counts.get(pfx, 0) + 1

    keys = set(mems.keys())
    cites_graph: dict[str, list[str]] = {}

    rows: list[dict[str, Any]] = []
    for key, body in mems.items():
        bead_refs = set(BEAD_RE.findall(body))
        bead_refs_full = {f"angr-{r}" for r in bead_refs}
        ref_statuses = {bead_status.get(b, "missing") for b in bead_refs_full}

        closed_only = bool(bead_refs_full) and ref_statuses <= {"closed", "missing"}
        open_ref = bool(ref_statuses & {"open", "in_progress", "blocked"})
        no_bead = not bead_refs_full

        status_shape = bool(STATUS_RE.search(body) or ITER_START_RE.match(body))

        docs_shape = len(body) >= 800 and bool(DOCS_LANG_RE.search(body))

        dates = DATE_RE.findall(body)
        future_date = any(int(y) == 2026 and int(m) >= 8 for (y, m, _) in dates) \
                      or any(int(y) > 2026 for (y, _, _) in dates)
        most_recent = max(("-".join(d) for d in dates), default="")
        stale_date = bool(most_recent and most_recent < "2026-05-01" and status_shape)

        # cites-other-memory: look for backticked keys
        cited = []
        for m in re.findall(r"`([a-z0-9][a-z0-9_-]{6,})`", body):
            if m in keys and m != key:
                cited.append(m)
        # also raw mentions of well-known keys
        for cand in keys:
            if len(cand) >= 12 and cand != key and cand in body:
                if cand not in cited:
                    cited.append(cand)
        if cited:
            cites_graph[key] = sorted(set(cited))

        cites_other = bool(cited)

        # dup-of-claude-md / dup-of-docs
        frags = _fragments(body)
        dup_claude = any(f in claude_md for f in frags) if frags else False
        dup_docs = any(f in docs_text for f in frags) if frags else False

        reference_type = key.startswith(REF_TYPE_PREFIXES)
        user_preference = bool(USER_PREF_RE.search(body))

        stale_file_ref = False
        for path in FILE_PATH_RE.findall(body):
            if path not in repo_files:
                # try a basename match before declaring stale (file may have moved)
                basename = path.rsplit("/", 1)[-1]
                if not any(rf.endswith("/" + basename) or rf == basename
                           for rf in repo_files):
                    stale_file_ref = True
                    break

        pfx = key.split("-")[0]
        rows.append({
            "key": key,
            "length": len(body),
            "prefix": pfx,
            "cluster_size": prefix_counts[pfx],
            "closed_only": int(closed_only),
            "open_ref": int(open_ref),
            "no_bead": int(no_bead),
            "status_shape": int(status_shape),
            "docs_shape": int(docs_shape),
            "future_date": int(future_date),
            "stale_date": int(stale_date),
            "cites_other": int(cites_other),
            "dup_of_claude_md": int(dup_claude),
            "dup_of_docs": int(dup_docs),
            "reference_type": int(reference_type),
            "user_preference": int(user_preference),
            "stale_file_ref": int(stale_file_ref),
            "most_recent_date": most_recent,
        })

    PRUNE_DIR.mkdir(exist_ok=True)
    with TRIAGE_CSV.open("w") as f:
        w = csv.DictWriter(f, fieldnames=list(rows[0].keys()))
        w.writeheader()
        w.writerows(rows)

    CITES_JSON.write_text(json.dumps(cites_graph, indent=2, sort_keys=True))

    # summary
    def cnt(field):
        return sum(r[field] for r in rows)

    print(f"Wrote {TRIAGE_CSV} ({len(rows)} rows)")
    print(f"Wrote {CITES_JSON} ({len(cites_graph)} citing memories, "
          f"{sum(len(v) for v in cites_graph.values())} citations)")
    print()
    print("Tag totals:")
    for field in ("closed_only", "open_ref", "no_bead", "status_shape",
                  "docs_shape", "future_date", "stale_date", "cites_other",
                  "dup_of_claude_md", "dup_of_docs", "reference_type",
                  "user_preference", "stale_file_ref"):
        print(f"  {field:20s} {cnt(field):5d}")
    return 0


if __name__ == "__main__":
    raise SystemExit(main())

=== v5a5-ais3-wins-opt-in ===
DURING v5a5 slice 4c.3 step 2 canary measurement (2026-05-24 iter 6, angr-awqp), ais3_crackme was the ONE canary that WON under use_shared_lineage_solver=True: 0.88s -> 0.71s (1.24x faster, 5-sample median). The other three regressed or were neutral (baby-re 6.79x slower, unbreakable_0 1.53x slower, r100 flat). This is the FIRST positive workload signal for the lineage-shared trunk on a real bench. Reason unknown — ais3 has very few states (1-2 active at a time) and short BFS depth, so the BFS-thrash that kills baby-re may simply not happen. Potential follow-up: profile ais3 with the opt-in flag to find the predictor (e.g. active-state count distribution, fork depth, query interleaving pattern) that distinguishes WIN workloads from LOSE workloads. If the predictor is cheap to compute at runtime, runtime-thrash-detection (alternative (c) in angr-3ms1) becomes viable.

=== v5a5-alt-a-lifo-hypothesis ===
alt-a (engine-level per-state query batching) for the v5a5 lineage architecture likely reduces to simply setting use_lifo=True (already a knob in RustExplorationManager). DESIGN PASS 2026-05-23 iter 10 (angr-3ms1 NOTES) found that with LIFO, push_to_active_or_drop pushes successors to back, pop_back retrieves the newest (a direct descendant of the last-stepped state). Consecutive states share a lineage chain → hot-cache hit rate ~100% → no push/pop thrash. The CURRENT BFS default (pop_front) interleaves across siblings, giving thrash. Next experiment: extend bench_lineage_push_pop_vs_assumptions in native/angr/benches/vex_engine.rs with a 'simulated LIFO pop order' variant. If LIFO variant matches per_state_batched (~13ms) instead of BFS-thrash (~32.7ms), Flavor-1 alt-a is confirmed cheaply. Without re-landing the reverted slice 4c.3 (fork-time lineage materialization), only the microbench can test this hypothesis on the main branch — production lineage fires only in the Callable path today. Flavor-2 (lineage-aware stash order) and Flavor-3 (K-step engine batching) are only needed if Flavor 1 doesn't work or BFS exploration order must be preserved.

=== v5a5-step-3a-predictor-2026-05-24 (2030 chars) ===
v5a5 slice 4c.3 step 3a (angr-1kqf, 2026-05-24 iter 7): profiled ais3_crackme (WIN 1.24x) vs defcon2016quals_baby-re (LOSE 6.79x slower, 4.07x peak mem) with --dump-counters under use_shared_lineage_solver. KEY NUMERIC DIFFERENCES between WIN and LOSE: (1) avoided_count 0 (ais3) vs 13 (baby-re) — baby-re uses 'avoid' stash via solve.py: sm.explore(find=..., avoid=...) which keeps lineage frames alive on dropped states; (2) lineage_pop_count 24 (ais3) vs 0 (baby-re) — baby-re's BFS tree never collapses back to parents; (3) lineage_switch_hot_count/total ratio 44.7% (ais3) vs 30.2% (baby-re) — better hot-cache reuse on ais3; (4) peak mem growth 1.13x (ais3, +49MB) vs 4.07x (baby-re, +1027MB) — 30x ratio in absolute lineage memory overhead; (5) z3_ast_cache_hit 73 (ais3) vs 0 (baby-re) — categorical difference in solver-call repetition. WALL-TIME ACCOUNTING: ais3 saves 224ms in z3_check + 277ms eliminated z3_materialize, costs +251ms in run_loop overhead (net -200ms wall). baby-re saves 200ms in z3_check + 144ms in z3_materialize, costs +125ms in run_loop AND ~2500ms UNACCOUNTED — likely allocator/Z3 backend pressure from the +1GB lineage memory bloat (not charged to z3_check_time_ns). The dominant cost is invisible to current Rust counters. PREDICTOR CANDIDATES: (A) STATIC: 'avoid_addrs > 0' read off SimulationManager at explore() start — strong signal but brittle (many CTF workloads use avoid). (B) RUNTIME: sample lineage_switch_hot_count/lineage_switch_count after N steps and dismantle if <35%, OR sample lineage_pop_count/lineage_push_count and dismantle if <5%. (C) MEMORY: monitor peak_mem growth rate per state; dismantle if growth rate exceeds e.g. 30MB/state. Cleanest single static heuristic = 'avoid_addrs > 0'. Cleanest runtime heuristic = hot-cache-hit-rate threshold. Recommended next: angr-ua1i (DFS coupling step 3b) is the WRONG direction — both benches use default BFS, the win/lose flip is workload-shape not strategy. Should close ua1i and pivot to alt (c) thrash-detection per angr-3ms1.

=== v5a5-step-2-canary-2026-05-24 (1145 chars) ===
angr-awqp (v5a5 slice 4c.3 step 2 canary, 2026-05-24 iter 6) MEASURED with use_shared_lineage_solver=True via new --use-shared-lineage-solver flag on tests/benchmarks/run_single.py (commit e02bef6ac). 5-sample medians (baseline -> opt-in): defcon2016quals_baby-re 0.47s -> 3.19s (6.79x SLOWER, mem 283MB->1434MB), defcamp_r100 0.23s -> 0.23s (neutral, mem +7%), ais3_crackme 0.88s -> 0.71s (1.24x FASTER, mem +13%), google2016_unbreakable_0 0.94s -> 1.44s (1.53x slower, mem +25%). VERDICT: per the bead's explicit acceptance criteria ('if baby-re regresses by ANY amount, the design needs revision'), the flag MUST stay default-off. This reproduces the v5a5-slice-4c.3-retry-failed-bfs-thrash-fundamental finding from iter-3: BFS-thrash dominates the lineage cost on baby-re even with the hot-cache prep (caa07ebf5) and the literal slice-1c semantics (per-fork fresh lineage, no Arc-sharing between siblings). NOTABLE: ais3 actually WON 1.24x — the opt-in is workload-dependent rather than uniformly bad. Step 3 (next) should either (a) tie the flag to DFS so workload selection is automatic, or (b) profile why ais3 wins to find the predictor.

=== v5a5-slice-4c.3-needs-opt-in-flag (1121 chars) ===
Slice 4c.3 (angr-3ms1 Flavor-1 step 1) cannot be landed as an unconditional fork-time materialization, even with the bare_z3_push_depth gate. Reason: iter-3 already validated the gate (488/488 tests passed) but baby-re still regressed 10x because BFS thrash is fundamental to the workload. Any new re-land MUST: (1) add the bare_z3_push_depth correctness gate, AND (2) tie the materialization itself to an engine-level opt-in (e.g. a flag on RustExplorationManager or on SymContext) that defaults OFF, so BFS workloads keep the current None-lineage behavior. The exploration_strategy='dfs' kwarg landed in iter-12 (commit f7d0fa27a) is one place to wire this — when strategy='dfs', enable lineage materialization at construction. The CI gate (run_regression.py --rust-only --skip-bimodal --threshold 0.15) runs default BFS and would catch the 10x regression on baby-re — do NOT land an unconditional change. This makes slice 4c.3 a 3-piece change (correctness gate + opt-in flag + DFS wiring), not the 1-piece change implied by the design memo. Discovered 2026-05-23 iter 13 while assessing risk before claiming the bead.

=== v5a5-slice-4-blocker-analysis (1596 chars) ===

Calling 'bd remember <text> --key <name>' WITHOUT --key flag, when <text> looks like a key name (no spaces), bd silently UPDATES the memory whose key equals <text> with value = <text>, clobbering its content. Always pass --key explicitly when updating, and always pass the actual memory text as the positional arg. Reproduced 2026-05-23 iter 12: 'bd remember v5a5-bare-z3-push-depth-counter-design' (intended as a read) destroyed that memo. Workaround: use 'bd memories <key>' to read, 'bd memories <key> --json' for full body. Use 'bd remember "<content>" --key <name>' to write or update.
---
Don't run 'bd remember KEYNAME' without a body string — it silently replaces the existing memory's contents with the literal key. The correct form is 'bd remember "insight text" --key keyname' (positional arg is the body; --key controls the key). Same gotcha bites bd update --notes when its argument expansion fails silently (e.g. a python heredoc with bad backslash escaping that emits empty) — the bead's notes get REPLACED with whatever string materialized, including empty. Recovery: 'bd history <id> --json' shows previous notes content from prior commits; copy from there, write to a tmpfile, then 'bd update <id> --notes="$(cat /tmp/file.txt)"'. Witnessed 2026-05-22 iter 17 when 'bd remember v5a5-slice-3b-landed' turned the slice-3b memory body into the string 'v5a5-slice-3b-landed' itself, and a follow-up '--notes="$(... | python -c ...)"' with bad python escaping replaced angr-v5a5 notes with the slice-3c block alone (slice 2/3a/3b lost). Both recoverable from history.

content.content: WARNING: 'bd update <id> --notes <text>' OVERWRITES the entire NOTES field — it does NOT append. Hit on 2026-05-22 iter 18 (slice 3h) when I tried to add the slice 3h note to angr-v5a5 and lost all prior slice 2/3a-3g history. Recovered by reconstructing from bd memories v5a5-slice-3*-landed and writing a complete chronology back with one bd update --notes. How to apply: always read the current notes (bd show <id>), append the new content, then bd update --notes with the FULL combined string. Better still, before update, dump existing notes to a tempfile: bd show <id> | sed -n '/^NOTES/,/^PARENT\|^$/p'. Or use --notes only on first creation and accumulate slice history elsewhere (memory keys, commit messages). Same overwrite footgun likely applies to --description and --design.

=== v5a5-alt-a-lifo-hypothesis-confirmed ===
angr-3ms1 LIFO hypothesis CONFIRMED via microbench (commit 5e59ff48b, 2026-05-23). Two new variants added to bench_lineage_push_pop_vs_assumptions in native/angr/benches/vex_engine.rs: push_pop_lifo_chain (200-deep descendant chain, every switch_to is 0 pops + 1 push) and push_pop_lifo_dfs_tree (depth-8 binary tree DFS-preorder, siblings share FrameId prefixes, transitions amortized O(2) pops + O(2) pushes). Criterion 10-sample medians: push_pop_lifo_chain 10.3 ms (FASTER than per_state_batched 13.2 ms by 22%; 3.16x faster than BFS thrash 32.6 ms); push_pop_lifo_dfs_tree 13.0 ms (matches per_state_batched within 1%; 2.5x faster than BFS thrash). Per-state-solver baselines for LIFO workloads: chain 1.77 sec, dfs_tree 1.56 sec — both ~100-150x slower than the lineage variant, so the shared trunk dominates regardless of access pattern. NEXT STEP: re-land slice 4c.3 (fork-time lineage materialization, with the bare_z3_push_depth gate from *** REF *** memo to fix the fork-inside-push correctness bug), wire a Python-side use_lifo=True default for lineage workloads, and measure baby-re. If baby-re recovers to baseline (~0.72s) or better, Flavor-1 of angr-3ms1 alt-a is the right path. Flavor-2 (lineage-aware stash order) and Flavor-3 (K-step engine batching) remain unnecessary.

=== v5a5-iter5-confirmed-bfs-thrash-fundamental ===
iter 5 (2026-05-23) on rust-symex confirmed the v5a5-slice-4c.3-retry-failed-bfs-thrash-fundamental finding by independently re-implementing fork-time SharedLineageSolver materialization. Saw the EXACT same correctness failure (test_fork_inside_push_isolation: ctx_a.satisfiable() returns False after pop+add(z!=20)) that the *** REF *** memo predicts — without the bare push-depth gate, lineage materialization clobbers a bare-push frame and y==10 leaks from scope 1 to scope 0. The iter-3 memo explicitly says 'do NOT retry vanilla fork-time materialization expecting different perf — the hot-cache prep is verified necessary-but-insufficient.' iter 5 heeded that and reverted before re-running the bench canary. Filed angr-3ms1 capturing the four architectural alternatives (a) per-state query batching at engine level (b) per-state solvers with shared trunk (c) runtime thrash detection + lineage dismantle (d) Z3 check-with-assumptions instead of push/pop.

content.content:
=== avoid-z3-solver-translate-same-context ===
Z3_solver_translate (Solver::clone) is BLOCKED as a fork-acceleration strategy when source-context == dest-context: returns a solver with 0 assertions (per existing memory z3-solver-translate-same-context-bug-z3-solver). Even though native/z3-patched/src/solver.rs:663 still wraps Z3_solver_translate via Solver::clone, the same-context bug rules out using it for SymContext::fork() — which is the path we'd want to optimize. Future hk7k attempts must NOT propose clone-based fork as a solution; the spike must use either shared-solver-with-push/pop (Option A) or per-state cross-context translate (Option D, expensive due to AST replication). Validated 2026-05-21 during angr-hk7k research spike.

=== build-z3-header-resolution ===
**Z3 header discovery for builds.** Z3 headers (`z3.h`) are NOT in the `z3-solver` PyPI wheel (it ships `libz3.so` only, under `z3/lib/`). The `z3-sys` crate needs headers to generate bindings.

**Discovery order** (in `setup.py::_resolve_z3_header`): (1) venv `z3/include/z3.h`, (2) `pkg-config --variable=includedir z3`, (3) `/usr/include`, `/usr/local/include`, `/opt/homebrew/include`, `/opt/local/include`. Sets `Z3_SYS_Z3_HEADER` before cargo runs. If nothing matches, prints an install hint (apt/dnf/brew) to stderr and lets z3-sys fall back to its own pkg-config probe.

**Install OS dev package** when build fails with `NotExist ... z3.h`:

Decision (angr-vulw, 2026-06-03): RustPosixProxy will NOT add dump_fd(fd, target_fd) (writeback-to-real-OS-fd) API in v1.0. Reason: Python angr's SimSystemPosix has no such API either — it exposes dumps(fd) -> bytes and dump_file_by_path(path) only. Adding dump_fd would be a Rust-only convenience that breaks behavioral parity (the contract that lets RustExplorationManager drop in for SimulationManager). Recommended caller workaround: data = state.posix.dumps(fd); os.write(target_fd, data) — one line, works on both engines. Documented in docs/advanced-topics/rust_engine.rst v1.0 scope section (lines 113-131 as of commit c5c8b6d8b). Companion to decision-v1-single-threaded (angr-02m1, iter 57) and decision-v1-no-real-multiprocess (angr-uw2y, iter 58).
---
v1.0 scope decision (angr-02m1, 2026-06-03): the Rust engine ships single-threaded. Rationale: three independent architectural constraints block parallel exploration: (1) Rc<RefCell<SymContext>> in RustSimState requires Send+Sync refactor of every fork site, (2) z3-rs 0.19+ thread-local Z3 contexts mean AST handles are bound to creating thread (cross-thread shipping requires SMT-LIB serialization round-trip), (3) intentional thread_local! AST caches in claripy_bridge.rs (4 caches). Two shortcuts proven non-viable: Z3 parallel.enable=true is correctness-breaking on 4 of 6 sampled benches (angr-gfay, avoid-z3-parallel-enable), and Rc->Arc + RefCell->Mutex alone does not lift Z3 thread-locality. Recommended v2 path: snapshot-transport via the already-Send+Sync ExplorationStateSnapshot type (angr-zidj). Multi-process is also v1.0 out of scope — users distribute via fuzzer-driven orchestration (libafl). Doc lives in docs/advanced-topics/rust_engine.rst::v1.0 scope, with full audit detail in the Concurrency / Send-Sync audit section (angr-8fo6) below it. Closes angr-02m1.
